title: Connectivity stack Terraform module for private deployments
creator: Asha Kapoor
description:
Purpose:
Build a single opinionated Terraform module (connectivity-stack) to provision VPC networking for Redwood Private deployments. The module must support multiple AZs, separate control and workload subnets, flexible egress architectures (NAT Gateway or centralized NAT instances or IGW), VPC endpoints (interface and gateway) with fine-grained policies, and route table orchestration.

Scope and constraints:
- Target use: Private (VPC) deployments for on-prem and cloud private control-plane variants.
- IaC: Terraform 1.4+ compatibility, providers pinned via lockfile; module follows Root Module pattern with clear inputs/outputs.
- Backward compatibility: default behaviors must match current deployments for existing customers; provide explicit migration paths for non-default configurations.
- Observability & health: include optional Lambda-based health probes for NAT/endpoint reachability, and a small telemetry module to register health metrics to CloudWatch / Prometheus remote write.
- Security: support endpoint policies and customer-supplied KMS keys for endpoint encryption where applicable. All sensitive outputs must be suppressed unless explicitly requested.
- Testing: include a terratest harness and an example root module for staging to validate drift, upgrades, and rollback.

Key design decisions to be implemented in module:
1) Subnet scheme: allow two logical tiers per AZ — control_subnets (for management plane) and workload_subnets (for model serving). Each will accept CIDR prefix lists and tag conventions.
2) Egress modes: enum var (egress_mode) with values ["nat-gateway","central-nat","internet-gateway","none"]. When central-nat selected, module will create a shared NAT subnet with a route table and optional autoscaling NAT instances using Launch Templates; for nat-gateway, create one per AZ with allocation optimization.
3) Endpoints: support aws_vpc_endpoint (gateway for S3/Dynamo) and aws_vpc_endpoint_service (interface) with per-endpoint policy attachment. Provide option to enable private DNS.
4) Routing: generate route tables per subnet type and AZ with configurable propagation and explicit route priorities. Route table attachment must be deterministic to support drift detection.
5) Upgrade path: include step-by-step migration scripts for users on older network module shapes (mapping of old resource names to new ones), and a zero-downtime token:canary toggle to move traffic between old and new route tables.
6) Outputs: export subnet ids grouped by AZ and tier, route table ids, endpoint ids, and a minimal JSON map of configuration for Redwood Console to consume.

Non-goals:
- Do not attempt to support every cloud provider in this module. Focus on AWS first.
- Do not bundle provider credentials or deployment automation beyond example roots and CI bits.

Acceptance and rollback strategy will be part of the deployment docs included with the module.
acceptance_criteria: Module provisions multi-AZ control and workload subnets with correct tags and CIDR allocations
Supports egress_mode variable with functional NAT Gateway and central NAT instance flows
Creates and manages gateway and interface VPC endpoints and attaches provided policies
Route tables per AZ and subnet type are deterministic and attach correctly
Module exposes outputs required by private operator bootstrap (subnet_map, endpoints, route_tables)
Automated terratest suite passes in staging (create/destroy/upgrade) without manual intervention
Migration guide included that maps old resource names to new ones and documents safe upgrade steps
Health probes detect NAT and endpoint failures and emit telemetry/alerts in staging
tasks: Design brief + schema for module inputs/outputs (done)
Implement core resources: VPC, subnets, route tables, IGW/NAT gateways
Implement egress_mode central-nat flow and autoscaling NAT instance option
Implement VPC endpoints with policy attachment and private DNS toggle
Add deterministic route table attachment logic and tagging conventions
Create terratest harness and CI job (GitHub Actions) for staging runs
Write migration scripts and upgrade playbook; include sample terraform state rename steps
Add optional health-check Lambda and CloudWatch metrics exporter
Code review, security review, and run in staging followed by canary to prod
